auditedPrs.notes: Squash 84f399d. Re-read against cmd/tailscaled/tailscaled.go and feature/condregister/maybe_bird.go at v1.102.4 (the diff cites older ref 53a0d659; the guard and Fatalf are unchanged at the pin). The message change does what it says: Go's sentence now sits whole on line 1, with the path moved below it. Two divergences remain, both disclosed. The flag is refused on every platform (engine-side: no BIRD hook), and line 1 keeps an error: prefix, a full stop and build text in place of GOOS.

Squash 4dce9c2; one row covers both beads on this PR. Matches Go in four ways: SelfChange has no mask bit, goes to every watcher, rides the initial frame only under NotifyInitialNetMap, and omits a key that never expires. But self_change hangs off the engine's peer tick, not a full netmap. So there is no frame when only this node changes, there are frames on delta-only responses, self is fetched late with a 500 ms timeout, and the payload is a 5-field subset.

Squash a787db8. The core is right: set and check-prefs judge the merged pref (Go's ApplyEdits then checkPrefsLocked), and check-prefs now reports auto-update before routes. Four divergences remain: set ordering and first-error stop, the config-load refusal, the refusal text, and up never checking. The diff discloses two of them, as a DECISION and a QUESTION.

Squash a38687b. Matches Go's prefsFromUpArgs and tailcfg.CheckTag: clause order, the four reason strings word for word, the tag: %q: %s frame, the tag: completion only when there is no colon, and the first-offender return. One divergence: Rust's {:?} is not Go's %q for control bytes.

Squash a8b5fbf. The four retagged refusals match Go byte for byte, and they now print bare as Go's main does (Fprintln then exit 1). The surrounding serve/funnel error surface still diverges: the --service refusals, daemon-stage errors, the check order pinned by the new tests, and %q quoting of the mount point.

Squash c872cca. Every interrupted run now exits 0, and the pref is restored only under Go's !cgi && startedManagementClient guard. One divergence: the interrupt handler is armed after the pref step, and the new doc comment claims the opposite. Not counted against this PR, because it predates it: a CGI write failure exits 1, where Go logs the cgi.Serve error and returns nil.

Squash 3977ad9; one row covers both beads on this PR. reload_and_publish faithfully ports the tail of reloadNow: swap and compare under the lock, notify only on change, single sender, both callbacks hung off it. Two divergences, both disclosed and not observable today: the first load publishes a change, and the comparison runs over redacted rendered rows.

Squash ddd2fb8, docs only (it rewrote PARITY_AUDIT.json for #459-#482). Its Go paths exist at the pin, and spot checks of the #476, #480 and #472 findings hold. Three findings are wrong or stale: #459's Start: prefix, #466's stopped-node output, and #482's tag wording, which #538 had already fixed. Separately, its commit body's totals (4 faithful, 7 findings) disagree with the file it merged (2 faithful, 14 findings).

gate.detail: On main at 877814d, with CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4, RUST_TEST_THREADS=4, TS_RS_EXPERIMENT=this_is_unstable_software, on the stable 1.95.0 toolchain (the box's default nightly has no clippy component; CI uses stable). cargo fmt --all --check and cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings: green. cargo test --all-targets: the first run failed one test, tailnetd tests::cleanup_refuses_live_socket, with `path must be shorter than SUN_LEN`. That is an environment cause, not a code one: darwin's 104-byte sun_path and a 66-char session TMPDIR. Rerun with a short private TMPDIR: 42 targets, 1267 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored. cargo build --release --bins: green.

findings.title: No self_change frame is sent when only this node changed
findings.detail: Go's setControlClientStatusLocked builds Notify{SelfChange: st.NetMap.SelfNode} on every full netmap, and map.go takes the full-netmap path whenever resp.Node changes. The merged stream_notify (src/server.rs) fetches self only when the engine ticks net_map, and the engine ticks only on peer, patch or liveness deltas. So a key-expiry extension, a rename or new self addresses produce no frame. Disclosed and filed as an engine ask, so the fix is engine-side.

findings.title: The two --service refusals print through a serve|funnel via <socket> / Caused by chain, not Go's single line
findings.detail: Go returns errors.New("Error: --service flag is not supported with funnel") and "Error: --service flag is only compatible with background mode", and main prints each bare on one line. The Rust literals carry no prefix, and main wraps every serve/funnel result in .with_context("serve via|funnel via <socket>") (src/bin/tnet.rs:2966-2971). Stderr is therefore an anyhow Error:/Caused by: block. The new test the_two_service_refusals_are_left_as_they_were pins that divergent output.

findings.title: --bird-socket is refused on every platform; Go accepts it on linux, darwin, freebsd and openbsd
findings.detail: Go fatals only when buildfeatures.HasBird && birdSocketPath != "" && !wgengine.HookNewBird.IsSet(). maybe_bird.go registers the hook under !ts_omit_bird && (linux||darwin||freebsd||openbsd), so the default build accepts the flag and passes it on as wgengine.Config.BIRDSocket. The merged can_use_bird() (src/bin/tailnetd.rs) always returns Err. Disclosed; the root cause is that the pinned engine has no BIRD hook, so the fix is engine-side.

findings.title: The --bird-socket refusal keeps an error: prefix, a full stop and build text where Go prints one bare GOOS line
findings.detail: Go runs log.SetFlags(0) and log.Fatalf("--bird-socket is not supported on %s", runtime.GOOS): stderr is exactly `--bird-socket is not supported on linux`, exit 1. The merged line 1 is `error: --bird-socket is not supported on this platform or in this build of tailnetd.`, followed by advice paragraphs. Disclosed in the doc comment. A substring match works, but a match anchored at line start or on Go's whole line does not.

findings.title: self_change is sent on delta-only map responses, where Go sends none
findings.detail: Go handles incremental responses (peer patches, online or last-seen changes) through tryHandleIncrementally and UpdateNetmapDelta, and returns before UpdateFullNetmap. That Notify never carries SelfChange. The pinned engine re-publishes its peer watch on liveness-only and patch-only responses, and the merged code decorates each resulting net_map frame with self_change. The rustdoc redefines the field as 'the netmap moved'; Go's backend.go defines it as this node's own Node changing. Not disclosed.

findings.title: The self node is read after the tick, not taken from the netmap being announced
findings.detail: Go takes SelfNode under b.mu from the same netmap it announces, both on updates and in the initial notify, and leaves it nil only when SelfNode is invalid. The merged fetch_self_report (src/ipn/mod.rs) calls dev.self_node() separately after the tick, bounded by the 500 ms STATUS_QUERY_TIMEOUT. Self can therefore come from a different netmap than the peers in the same frame, and a timeout or error ships the frame with no self.

findings.title: SelfReport is a 5-field subset of tailcfg.Node and always rides with the full peer list
findings.detail: Go's Notify.SelfChange is a whole *tailcfg.Node: all Addresses, the FQDN Name with its trailing dot, CapMap, Tags, User and so on. On non-Windows, runtime SelfChange frames carry no NetMap. The merged SelfReport (src/localapi.rs) has stable_id, a display name, one ipv4, one ipv6 and key_expiry, and every frame that carries it also carries the full net_map. The subset is disclosed as a decision.

findings.title: set checks advertise-routes before auto-update and stops at the first error
findings.detail: Go's editPrefsLocked calls checkPrefsLocked(p1), which collects every violation with errors.Join in a fixed order: SSH, exit node, funnel, checkAutoUpdatePrefsLocked, checkAdvertiseRoutes. The merged begin_set_gated (src/ipn/mod.rs) runs validate_advertise_routes(...)? first and returns on the first failure. A set that breaks both rules reports only the route error, in reverse of Go's order. The diff reordered only check_prefs.

findings.title: A config-file AutoUpdate.Apply opt-in fails the whole config load; Go accepts it
findings.detail: Go's initPrefsFromConfig and setConfigLocked run ToPrefs, ApplyEdits and SetPrefs/setPrefsLocked, never checkPrefsLocked, so a Go daemon boots with the opt-in. The merged Config::apply_to_prefs (src/conffile.rs) refuses the config with `config: AutoUpdate.Apply: ...`, so tailnetd does not start on a host that cannot update. Disclosed as a deliberate DECISION.

findings.title: The auto-update refusal text is not Go's sentence
findings.detail: Go's checkAutoUpdatePrefsLocked returns exactly `Auto-updates are not supported on this platform.`, or `Auto-update support is disabled in this build` behind the build gate. The merged src/ipn/selfupdate.rs keeps Go's sentence only as a prefix, then appends an explanation, an AllowsUpdate sentence and a remedy the caller chooses. Its Homebrew branch says `...not supported on this installation: ...`. The build-gate message has no counterpart.

findings.title: up never checks the auto-update pref, so a stored opt-in does not fail up as it does in Go
findings.detail: Go's Start runs checkPrefsLocked on opts.UpdatePrefs, and a running node's tailscale up goes through EditPrefs, so a persisted opt-in on a host that cannot update fails up. The merged begin_up_gated (src/ipn/mod.rs) validates only routes and tags. check_auto_update_pref is called only from set, check_prefs and the config loader. The title says 'every ingress'; this one is left out, though the diff raises it as a QUESTION.

findings.title: Tag refusals quote with Rust {:?}, which differs from Go's %q for control bytes
findings.detail: Go formats the refusal as fmt.Errorf("tag: %q: %s", tag, err), and strconv.Quote writes 0x01 as \x01, 0x7f as \x7f and NUL as \x00. The merged complete_and_validate_advertise_tags (src/ipn/mod.rs) uses {t:?}, which writes \u{1}, \u{7f} and \0. CheckTag's last clause rejects exactly these bytes, so `tag:a` followed by 0x01 reaches this frame and prints differently from tailscale up. The commit claims the output is identical for every string CheckTag can reach.

findings.title: Daemon-stage serve/funnel errors still print as Error: ... via <socket> plus Caused by
findings.detail: Go prints everything else runServeCombined returns bare: `error getting serve config: %w`, `getting client status: %w`, `service hosts must be tagged nodes`, `missing SessionID`. In Rust all of them pass through the same main-level with_context wrapper (src/bin/tnet.rs) and anyhow's Termination rendering, so each gains a header and a Caused by block that Go never prints.

findings.title: New integration tests pin a check order that puts the PROXY refusals before Go's funnel check
findings.detail: For funnel, Go calls verifyFunnelEnabled(ctx, 443), which talks to the daemon, before cleanURLPath and the PROXY-protocol checks. Its tun refusal comes after GetServeConfig and the status call. Rust has no verifyFunnelEnabled and decides all four retagged refusals before touching the socket. tests/serve_refusal_stderr_framing.rs asserts `tnet funnel --proxy-protocol=1 3000` prints the PROXY refusal with no daemon, a case where Go fails at the daemon first.

findings.title: The mount-point refusal quotes the path with {:?}, not Go's %q
findings.detail: Go's cleanURLPath error quotes the path with %q, so ESC renders as \x1b. The merged mount-point refusal formats it with {with_slash:?} (src/bin/tnet.rs), so ESC renders as \u{1b}. The PR says this sentence is now Go's exactly, which holds only for printable paths. The quoting itself predates the PR.

findings.title: The web interrupt handler is armed after the pref step, not as runWeb's first statement
findings.detail: Go's runWeb opens with signal.NotifyContext(ctx, os.Interrupt), before StatusWithoutPeers, GetPrefs and setRunWebClient(ctx, true). A SIGINT in that window cancels the context or reaches the restore goroutine, then exits 0. The merged run_web (src/bin/tnet.rs) awaits start_tailscaled_web_client first, and tokio::signal::ctrl_c() installs its handler only when first polled in serve_until_interrupt. So a SIGINT during the pref step exits 130 and may leave RunWebClient on. The new doc on web_interrupt says it is armed before the pref step.

findings.title: The first policy load publishes a change, which Go's reloadNow suppresses
findings.detail: Go's reloadNow fires the change callbacks only under `old != nil && !old.EqualItems(new)`, so a scope's first resolution notifies nobody. The merged LAST_PUBLISHED (src/ipn/syspolicy.rs) starts as an empty Vec, so the first load_json_policy_file that sets any key publishes a tick. Disclosed; not observable today because the file loads before the LocalAPI serves.

findings.title: The change test compares redacted rendered rows, where Go deep-hashes the raw items
findings.detail: Go's Snapshot.EqualItems compares the length, then a deephash of the raw item map, including the real AuthKey. The merged reload_and_publish compares Vec<PolicySetting> rows in which AuthKey is rendered <redacted>, so a change that only rotates the AuthKey would notify in Go but not here. Disclosed; unreachable today because only one source is ever registered, once.

findings.title: The #459 finding says Go's syspolicy AuthKey skip line has no Start: prefix; it does
findings.detail: Go's Start sets logf := logger.WithPrefix(b.logf, "Start: "), and both the `not setting opts.AuthKey from syspolicy` line and the `setting opts.AuthKey by syspolicy, len=%v` line go through it. The finding ddd2fb8 committed against #459 says upstream's line has no Start: prefix. The rest of that finding is accurate.

findings.title: The #466 finding misstates Go's tailscale ip output on a stopped node
findings.detail: The finding says Go prints `no current Tailscale IPs; state: Stopped` for a node that has run down. But Go's Status takes TailscaleIPs from the netmap, and entering Stopped only reconfigures the engine with an empty config. The netmap is cleared only by resetForProfileChangeLocked, so a stopped node that still holds a netmap prints its addresses. The Rust divergence reported (`error: node is not up`) is still real.

findings.title: The #482 tag-wording finding describes code already fixed on main when the audit merged
findings.detail: The finding says tag refusals are reworded (`invalid tag ...: tags must be of the form ...`). But #538 (a38687b, an ancestor of ddd2fb8) had already switched src/ipn/mod.rs to Go's `tag: %q: %s` frame and the four CheckTag sentences word for word. A reader following this row would chase a divergence that was already fixed.
